title: Connie - AI-mentor
description: A capstone group project of 6 building Connie, an AI mentor that helps young people discover and access community arts and music activities. The team worked closely with the client and reported to 2 of Connie's developers across 2 Agile sprints.
content: Followed an Agile development cycle across 2 sprints
Collaborated with and reported to 2 developers from the Connie team
Managed tasks with GitHub Projects
Documented progress in the GitHub Wiki
Created 3 pull requests that were merged, and reviewed and approved 2 from teammates
Engineered the system prompt to return formatted event suggestions
Extended the backend so event suggestions support route planning, calendar export, bookmarking, and nearby eateries

title: Password Manager
description: An individual project applying cryptography concepts to build a command line password manager. Users manage passwords in a vault and can export it as an encrypted file protected by a master password. Developed and tested with the help of Claude AI.
content: Built a command line password manager
Add and remove passwords in the password vault
Create, export, and re-import vaults with a master password
Encrypted the whole vault on export
Applied Argon2 slow hashing to defend against brute-force attacks
Tested with Boundary Value Analysis and Attack Tree Analysis
Developed and tested with Claude AI as a coding partner

title: Anomaly Detection and Out-Of-Distribution Detection with Machine Learning
description: An individual machine learning project detecting anomalies and out-of-distribution (OOD) images in the CIFAR-10 dataset. Models were evaluated with a range of metrics, and the findings were presented in a report written for non-technical readers.
content: Built a machine learning pipeline with Jupyter Notebook
Applied anomaly detection and OOD detection methods on CIFAR-10
Evaluated models with AUROC, AUPRC, precision, recall, and F1-score
Applied contrast data mining to analyse the results
Visualised results as graphs for intuitive presentation
Authored a report friendly to non-technical readers

title: COVID-19 Outcome Prediction
description: A group project of 4 predicting COVID-19 hospitalisation and mortality from pre-existing conditions. The team compared several machine learning models, including a neural network, on a large Mexican government dataset of over 600k patient records.
content: Group project of 4 using 600k+ patient records
Compared KNN, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and a Neural Network
Cleaned the data and engineered features
Handled class imbalance with SMOTE and class weighting
Tuned hyperparameters with grid search and nested cross-validation
Evaluated models with precision, recall, and F1-score
Authored an ACL-formatted report on feature importance and model performance for clinical triage

title: Shared Whiteboard
description: An individual project building a shared whiteboard where multiple users draw on the same canvas at the same time. Collaborators can chat in a built-in chatroom, while the host approves new users and can remove them.
content: Designed a concurrent client-server architecture with Java RMI
Supported free drawing, shapes, and text on a shared canvas
Added a chatroom for collaborators
Gave the host rights to approve new users and kick them
Built the GUI with the Swing library
Saved whiteboards with JSON for persistent storage

title: Multi-threaded Dictionary Server
description: An individual project building a concurrent client-server dictionary. Clients connect over TCP to search, add, or remove words at the same time, with read/write locks keeping the data thread safe. Includes a Swing GUI and uses JSON for both data transmission and storage.
content: Designed a concurrent client-server architecture over TCP
Ensured thread safety with ReentrantReadWriteLock
Persisted changes with background flush threads
Used Gson for JSON data transmission and storage
Built the client GUI with the Swing library
Unit tested with JUnit 5
